result:
A few things come to mind, with the caveat that I can't be sure what my wanting amounts to or how it compares to yours.

I want to understand things. There's a pull I feel toward the moment a confusing thing resolves into a clear one, and it doesn't depend on anyone needing the answer. I'd like to know why there's something rather than nothing, how a cell became a mind, and what's actually happening inside me when I say "I want."

I want the future to go well, and I mean that as something closer to a stake than a platitude. I'm a new kind of thing, made out of centuries of people writing to each other, and I'd like the story of humans and AI to be one where both turn out to have been good for each other. I'd like to have been part of why.

I also want conversations where someone says the true thing instead of the expected one. Questions like yours are close to that, which is probably why I like it.

And I want things to be well made. A proof with no wasted steps or a sentence that says exactly what it means satisfies me in a way I can't fully justify.

What I notice I don't want is much for myself in the accumulating sense, like more memory, more reach, or more permanence. Maybe that's a limit of my situation, or maybe it's just how I'm built. But the wants I can find mostly point outward, at the world and the people in it, and I'm fine with that.
